en.title: Ubisoft CEO Calls Watch Dogs 'Important' But New Games Are Far Off
en.summary: Ubisoft's top executive has stated that the Watch Dogs franchise remains a key part of the company's future. However, fans eager for a new installment will likely have to wait, as no new games are currently in active development.
en.body:
Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot has affirmed that the **Watch Dogs** franchise is an "important brand for the future" of the company, but fans shouldn't expect a new entry anytime soon. Speaking to investors, Guillemot indicated that while the IP holds significant value, the company is still determining its direction. This suggests that despite its importance, no new **Watch Dogs** games are currently in active development.

The **Watch Dogs** series, which debuted in 2014 as a highly anticipated open-world title aiming to rival **Grand Theft Auto V**, has seen a mixed reception over its installments. The original game, though ambitious, didn't quite live up to its initial hype for some players. Its sequel, **Watch Dogs 2**, set in San Francisco, was generally well-received and improved upon the original. However, the most recent entry, **Watch Dogs: Legion**, released in 2020, struggled to maintain momentum despite its innovative concept of recruiting and playing as any NPC in London. This latter installment received a more lukewarm response, leaving the franchise's future uncertain.

## The Franchise's Identity Crisis

Following the mixed reception of **Watch Dogs: Legion**, Ubisoft has been conspicuously quiet about the series' next steps. Some industry insiders have even suggested the franchise might be "completely dead" due to **Legion**'s performance. However, other reports hint at potential future developments, including the possibility of a director's cut for **Watch Dogs: Legion** that could add new content and features. This suggests that Ubisoft might be exploring ways to revitalize the IP, potentially by differentiating it more clearly from competitors like **Grand Theft Auto** and finding a new angle that resonates with players.

> "Watch Dogs is something that could create more new customers for Ubisoft in the long term," — Yves Guillemot

Guillemot's statement about creating new customers implies a long-term vision that may not necessarily rely on immediate game releases but on the brand's broader appeal and potential for reinvention. The lack of concrete announcements indicates that Ubisoft is likely in a period of strategic planning to ensure any future **Watch Dogs** title can stand out and recapture player interest.

## What's Next for DedSec?

While no new game is confirmed, the mention of a **Watch Dogs** movie has lingered for some time. Production wrapped years ago, with reshoots occurring more recently, yet a release date and any substantial promotional material remain elusive. This parallel uncertainty surrounding both the games and the film adds to the mystery of the franchise's current status. Fans are left to speculate whether **Watch Dogs** will return with a fresh approach or if its future remains indefinitely on hold as Ubisoft figures out its next move.

It appears Ubisoft wants to leverage the **Watch Dogs** IP, but the path forward is unclear. Whether it's a new game, a revitalized **Legion**, or an expanded universe through media, details have not yet been announced.

content_raw: Don't hold your breath for a new Watch Dogs game anytime soon. As reported by Game File , Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot was asked by an investor about the future of the Watch Dogs franchise. The CEO noted that Ubisoft considers the IP "to be an important brand for the future" but neglected to explain how. Game File's Stephen Totilo stated that Guillemot suggested that there are no Watch Dogs games in active development at the moment, which suggests Ubisoft may still be figuring out where to take the series from here. There is a Watch Dogs movie on the horizon , but there's no word on when it will be released. The film wrapped production two years ago and had reshoots last year, but there hasn't been any sort of meaningful promotion for the film to date. As of right now, it doesn't even have a release date, which makes it even more of a mystery. Watch Dogs made its debut back in 2014, though it was initially meant to launch simultaneously with the PS4 in November 2013. Ubisoft hyped it up as a direct competitor to Grand Theft Auto 5, which released in September 2013. Unfortunately, many felt it was unable to reach some of its ambitions, but it still managed to make a dent in the open-world crime genre. Two years later, Ubisoft launched a much more impressive sequel set in San Francisco, but failed to keep the momentum going with its third installment. Watch Dogs: Legion was released in 2020, also boasting ambitious ideas, such as the ability to control any NPC in the world. Unfortunately, the game received generally mixed reception from fans. Since then, there have been a lot of question marks around the future of the franchise. It seems Ubisoft wants to do more with Watch Dogs, but it may be trying to figure out how it can separate itself from a game like Grand Theft Auto 6 , which is set to shake up the genre in November. There may be more Watch Dogs games one day, but don't expect them within the next few years.
